newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's JSE falls to 16th place in world league.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's JSE falls to 16th place in world league.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange slipped to 16th place in the world stock exchange league in 1996 from 12th place in 1995, reflecting a dismal performance by the market in dollar terms.
JSE figures showed the combined market capitalisation of the 626 companies listed on the JSE in December 1996 fell to $241.6 billion from $277.4 a year earlier.
However, the market's turnover increased to $27.0 billion from $17.4, lifting liquidity to 11.2 percent in 1996 from 6.3 percent in 1995.

Ranked by dollar turnover, the JSE stands 29th among the 42 member stock exchanges of the Federation Internationale des Bourses de Valeurs. Its poor liquidity ratio, however, leaves in languishing in 38th position on that yardstick.
The JSE said there had been a further modest pick up in turnover and liquidity in the first month of 1997.

Turnover excluding arbitrage in January totalled 11.8 billion rand, 23 percent up on the same month of 1995, but little changed in dollar terms given the rand's sharp fall in 1996. Annualised liquidity stood at 12.4 percent in January.
